[[United States national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Melvin Anderson Ely''' ({{IPAc-en|iː|'|l|aɪ}}; born May 2, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who was also an assistant coach for the [[Cleveland Charge|Canton Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]]. A 6'10", {{convert|261|lb|abbr=on}}, [[power forward]]–[[center (basketball)|center]] from [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]], Ely was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the first round (12th overall pick) of the [[2002 NBA draft]]. At Fresno State, he enjoyed a prolific career under the coaching of [[Jerry Tarkanian]]. ==High school career== While attending [[Thornton Township High School|Harvey Thornton High School]], Ely earned All-American honors from [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's]] and [[Parade Magazine]]. As a senior in 1997, he averaged 15.5 points per game, 9.3 rebounds per game and 5.2 blocked shots per game during the regular season and was named the [[Chicago Sun-Times]] player of the year and first team [[Illinois High School Association|all-state]]. Ely led his Wildcats to a [[Illinois high school boys basketball championship#1992–2007|second-place]] finish in 1995 and 1996 and third-place in 1997. During Ely's 3 years as a starter, Thornton Township posted a combined record of 93 wins and 4 losses, including marks of 32–1 in 1997, 31–1 in 1996 and 30–2 in 1995.[http://www.ihsa.org/records/index.htm IHSA Record Book] 3 of those losses were to eventual IHSA 2A champions Peoria Manual. In 2007, Ely was voted one of the "[[100 Legends of the IHSA Boys Basketball Tournament]]", recognizing his superior performance in his appearances in the tournament.[http://www.ihsa.org/initiatives/legends/index.htm IHSA – Legends of Boys Basketball] ==College career== Under the guidance of coach [[Jerry Tarkanian]] at [[California State University, Fresno|Fresno State]], Ely led the Bulldogs to two NCAA tournament appearances in 2000 and 2001. Over his four‑year college career he played 124 games and averaged 15.7 points per game and 7.5 rebounds per game. He was a dominant presence at Fresno State: by the time he left, he had become the school’s all‑time leading scorer with 1,951 points, its leader in blocks with 362, and in total field goals made is 789. Ely earned top individual honors in college: he was named [[WBCA Player of the Year|WAC Player of the Year]] twice in 2001 and 2002. He also earned First‑Team All‑WAC selections, All‑Defense recognition in the WAC, and was a key contributor to the Bulldogs reaching the postseason multiple times including [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearances in 2000 and 2001. In his senior season 2001‑02, Ely averaged 23.3 points, 9.1 rebounds and 3.2 blocks per game one of the most impressive individual seasons in school history. Because of his outstanding performance and contributions, he was later inducted into the Fresno State Athletics Hall of Fame. ==Professional career== After two seasons in Los Angeles with limited playing time, Ely was traded by the Clippers along with teammate [[Eddie House]] on July 14, 2004, to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for two second-round draft picks in 2005 and 2006. During the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] and [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 seasons]], Ely rejuvenated his career as a prominent reserve role player. On October 2, 2006, he rejected offers from the [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Phoenix Suns]] to sign a one-year, $3 million contract to remain with the Bobcats.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2610570 ESPN – Ely signs one-year, $3 million offer with Bobcats – NBA] On February 13, 2007, he was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for forward [[Eric Williams (basketball, born 1972)|Eric Williams]] and a second-round draft pick in 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/melvin_ely_070213.html | title=Spurs Acquire Melvin Ely | work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 13, 2007 | access-date=December 15, 2011}} He played only 6 games for the Spurs, averaging 3.2 points and 2.3 rebounds per game. He did not play for the Spurs in the playoffs yet he still won the championship ring. In the 2007 off-season, Ely signed with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3016931 Report: Hornets sign free agent Ely to contract], September 13, 2007 It was formally announced on September 12 that it was a two-year contract.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3018235 Hornets hoping Ely can deliver on potential, add depth], September 13, 2007 In 2012, Ely 2014|newspaper=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2014}} Ely's final NBA game was April 16, 2014 in a 105 - 100 win over the [[Houston Rockets]] where he recorded 4 points and 1 block. On July 15, 2014, he was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]].[http://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-complete-three-team-trade Wizards Complete Three-Team Trade] On July 30, 2014, he was waived by the Wizards.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/wp/2014/07/30/wizards-waive-melvin-ely/ Wizards waive Melvin Ely][http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/129633/wizards-waive-melvin-ely.html Wizards waive Melvin Ely] In September 2014, Ely signed a one-year deal with the Gunma Crane Thunders of the Japanese [[bj league]].[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2014/09/melvin-signs-japanese.html Melvin Ely Signs With Japanese Team] On November 2, 2017, Ely was Inducted in to the Fresno Athletic Hall of Fame with some of his 2005 Fresno State teammates in attendance. ==Coaching career== On August 23, 2015, Ely was hired to join Martin Knezevic's staff in the newly-formed AmeriLeague in Las Vegas (league folded prior to the season).{{Cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/player/melvin-ely|title=Melvin Ely Rumors}} On September 27, 2016, he was hired by the [[Cleveland Charge|Canton Charge]] to serve as an assistant coach.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/coaching-staff-160927|title=Cavaliers Announce Coaching Staff for Cavs and Canton Charge|work=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | {{nbay|2002}} | align="left" | [[2002–03 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
